headline: Approved multiple special education staffing contracts, a $1,500 special education differential MOU, and a $91,600 grant from Crotched Mountain Foundation.
summary: The board approved the consent agenda and a series of contracts for special education and ELL staffing and services, including Clark Associates, ESS, Rockingham, SSG, SLP for Mama-to-be, Carroll Center, and Next Steps BHS. It also approved security and facility-use policies, personnel recommendations, an Ellevation Essential purchase, a memorandum of understanding on a special education pay differential, and a $91,600 grant from Crotched Mountain Foundation. Public comment focused on stipends for music and other co-curricular advisors.
decisions: Approved purchase of 330 digital licenses for HMH's English 3D program and related materials for ELL classes, not to exceed $33,000.00.
Approved updated contract with Clark Associates for the 2027 school year, not to exceed $1,061,483.00.
Approved contract addendum with ESS for one additional full-time MHT for 2026-2027, not to exceed $98,000.00.
Approved contract with Rockingham for 1.6 SLP positions for 2026-2027, not to exceed $211,680.00.
Approved contract with SSG for 1.0 SLP and 1.0 ASL Interpreter positions for 2026-2027, not to exceed $236,880.00.
Approved contract with SLP for Mama-to-be for part-time SLP leave coverage for 2026-2027, not to exceed $46,900.00.
Approved contract with Carroll Center for Orientation and Mobility services for 2026-2027, not to exceed $135,990.00.
Approved the FY27 July Transfer Reports.
Approved Policy ECA-R District Security Procedures.
Approved Policy KF Community Use of School Facilities.
Voted not to seal the non-public minutes, by roll call.
Approved purchase of Ellevation Essential from Curriculum Associates, not to exceed $81,948.75, with $52,514 from the operating budget and $18,928.63 from Title III.
Approved contract with Next Steps BHS for one full-time certified Special Education Teacher for 2026-2027, not to exceed $168,750.00.
Approved the Memorandum of Understanding on Eligibility of Special Education Differential between the Nashua Board of Education and the Nashua Teachers' Union, Unit A.
Approved the grant award from Crotched Mountain Foundation for the 2026-2029 CMF Kids Anchor Partnership Award, $91,600.00 for FY2027.

Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the updated contract with Clark Associates for the 2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $1,061,483.00. Funding to be charged to account 91.1.022160 53614. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with Rockingham for staffing of 1.6 SLP positions for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $211,680.00. Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the contract with SSG for staffing of 1.0 SLP position and 1.0 ASL Interpreter position for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $236,880.00. Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the contract with SLP for Mama-to-be for staffing of part-time SLP leave-coverage for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $46,900.00. Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the contract with Carroll Center for Orientation and Mobility services for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $135,990.00. Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Bishop, to not seal the non-public minutes. ... So voted by roll call at 7:15 pm.
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the August 24, 2026 Personnel Recommendations. Motion passes 8-0.

Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the purchase of Ellevation Essential from Curriculum Associates at a cost not to exceed $81,948.75, with $52,514 from operating budget and $18,928.63 from Title III. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Bishop, to approve the contract with Next Steps BHS for staffing one full-time certified Special Education Teacher for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $168,750.00. Funding to be charge to the Operating budget under Contracted Services. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Memorandum of Understanding “Eligibility of Special Education Differential” between the Nashua Board of Education and the Nashua Teachers’ Union, Unit A. Motion passes 9-0.

Ms. Lopez moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the grant award from Crotched Mountain Foundation for the 2026-2029 CMF Kids Anchor Partnership Award in the amount of $91,600.00 for FY2027. Motion passes 9-0.

BOARD OF EDUCATION 
MONDAY, AUGUST 24, 2026 
NHS NORTH BOARD ROOM 
 
A meeting of the Board of Education was held at NHS North on Monday, August 24, 2026.  Ms. Bishop 
called the meeting to order at 6:01 pm and asked Ms. Raymond to read the opening statement and Ms. Prinn 
to lead the Pledge of Allegiance. 
 
Present: Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Raymond, Ms. Lewis, Mr. Salvi, Ms. Lamphier,  
Ms. Lopez, Ms. Bishop 
 
Also Present:  Dr. Andrade, Dr. Scarpati, Ms. De Gray 
Also Present:  Members of the Public, Channel 99 Videographer 
 Student Representatives Alia Saad (North) arrived late 
 
CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Raymond, to approve the Consent Agenda.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
ITEMS REMOVED FROM CONSENT AGENDA 
 
COMMUNICATIONS OUTSIDE THE CONSENT AGENDA 
 
PUBLIC QUESTION/COMMENT PERIOD LIMITED TO ITEMS ON THIS AGENDA 
Gary Hoffman, NTU 
• Mr. Hoffman speaks about the memorandum of understanding for the eligibility of special education 
differentials, the importance of defining special educators, and the benefits of the $1,500 differential 
for special educators. 
 
SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Dr. Andrade welcomes students, families, faculty, and staff back to the 2026-2027 school year, 
emphasizing the district's strategic plan and mission. 
• Dr. Andrade outlines the theme "One Nashua, One Learning System" and the three principles of 
shared direction, shared learning, and shared responsibility. 
• Dr. Andrade acknowledges the hard work of various district teams, including plant operations, 
transportation, and the Welcome Center, in preparing for the new school year. 
 
BOARD RESPONSE TO SUPERINTENDENT’S COMMENTS 
• Board members express their hope and excitement for the new school year, wishing success to 
students, teachers, and staff. 
 
STUDENT REPRESENTATIVE COMMENTS 
 
COMMITTEE ON BUDGET 
 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE AND OPERATIONS 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the purchase of 330 digital licenses for HMH’s 
English 3D program, along with teacher digital license and two teacher guides for use in the high school 
ELL classes during the 2026-27 and 2027-2028 school years in an amount not to exceed $33,000.00.  
Motion passes 9-0.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  August 24, 2026 
 
 
2 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the updated contract with Clark Associates for the 
2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $1,061,483.00.  Funding to be charged to account 91.1.022160 
53614.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the contract addendum with ESS for staffing one 
additional full-time MHT for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $98,000.00.  Funding to be 
charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the contract with Rockingham for staffing of 1.6 
SLP positions for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $211,680.00.  Funding to be charged to 
the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• The board discussed the elevated cost of the two positions proposed in the SSG contract.  Board 
members inferred that the District does not pay enough.  Dr. Andrade clarifies salary and benefits and 
total cost of an employee.  He also noted that “not to exceed” means the rate/cost could be lower. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the contract with SSG for staffing of 1.0 SLP 
position and 1.0 ASL Interpreter position for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$236,880.00.  Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-
0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the contract with SLP for Mama-to-be for 
staffing of part-time SLP leave-coverage for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $46,900.00.  
Funding to be charged to the Operating Budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the contract with Carroll Center for Orientation 
and Mobility services for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $135,990.00.  Funding to be 
charged to the IDEA Grant for IEP students and the Operating Budget (Contracted Services) for students 
under 504 plan.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
Ms. Lamphier moved, seconded by Mr. Salvi, to approve the FY27 July Transfer Reports.  Motion passes 9-
0. 
 
COMMITTEE ON POLICY 
• Ms. Raymond discusses the public hearing held earlier this evening on the use of cameras on school 
buses and the need for compliance with the parental bill of rights. 
• The board decides to vote on the policy at the next meeting, ensuring compliance with state laws. 
• Ms. Raymond presents various policies for first reading, including updates to existing policies and 
new policies on discrimination and harassment. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy ECA District Security.  Motion passes 
9-0. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson, to approve Policy ECA-R District Security Procedures.  
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• Ms. Raymond presents policy KF for community use of school facilities, highlighting updates on 
priority access, charges, and additional ongoing costs. 
• The board discusses the importance of maintaining the quality of gym mats and the need for a special 
fund for replacements.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  August 24, 2026 
 
 
3 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Mr. Johnson to approve Policy KF Community Use of School Facilities.  
Motion passes 9-0. 
 
COMMITTEE ON HUMAN RESOURCES  
 
NEW BUSINESS 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Giglio, to enter non-public session at 7:00 pm under RSA 91-A:3II 
(b).

• Dr. Andrade thanks the HR department for processing over 250 new hires this summer. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Lopez, to approve the August 24, 2026 Personnel Recommendations.  
Motion passes 8-0. 
 
• Dr. Andrade requested the Board’s signatures on 2026 MS-26C – Nashua Local School Proposed 
Budget (no motion required) as well as the 2026 MS-22 – Nashua Local School – Report of 
Appropriations as voted (no motion required) 
• Dr. Andrade gives an overview of the Ellevation Essentials from Curriculum Associates (ELL 
program). 
• Ms. Raymond questions the grades for which the materials will be used, and Dr. Scarpati explains 
that it is a platform for K-12. 
• Ms. Prinn describes the platform's functionality, including data input and instructional 
recommendations based on WIDA CanDo descriptors. 
• Dr. Andrade explains the recommendation is part of the Department of Justice's guidelines for 
solidifying the curriculum and notes the success in moving students to monitor status. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the purchase of Ellevation Essential from 
Curriculum Associates at a cost not to exceed $81,948.75, with $52,514 from operating budget and 
$18,928.63 from Title III.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• Dr. Andrade introduces the contract with Next Steps BHS for staffing one full-time certified special 
education teacher for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed $168,750.
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  August 24, 2026 
 
 
9 
• Ms. Giglio questions the high cost, and Ms. Raymond expresses concern about the state's 
requirements and the high cost compared to other states. 
• Dr. Andrade explains the total compensation of teachers, including benefits and retirement, and the 
challenges in hiring special educators. 
• Dr. Scarpati mentions ongoing grant writing and the potential for better contract negotiations in the 
future. 
 
Ms. Raymond moved, seconded by Ms. Bishop, to approve the contract with Next Steps BHS for staffing 
one full-time certified Special Education Teacher for the 2026-2027 school year at a cost not to exceed 
$168,750.00.  Funding to be charge to the Operating budget under Contracted Services.  Motion passes 9-
0. 
 
 
• Dr. Andrade introduces a recommendation to approve the MOU eligibility of special education 
differential between the Nashua Board of Education and the Nashua Teachers Union Unit A. 
• Ms. Raymond expresses concern about the contrast between spending on contractors and the $1,500 
differential for special education teachers. 
• Ms. Lamphier suggests the possibility of increasing the differential in future negotiations. 
• Dr. Andrade and Ms. Bishop discuss the MOU's duration until the end of the teacher contract in 2029. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Memorandum of Understanding “Eligibility of 
Special Education Differential” between the Nashua Board of Education and the Nashua Teachers’ 
Union, Unit A.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
 
• Dr. Andrade introduces a recommendation to approve the grant award from Crotchet Mountain 
Foundation for the 2026-2029 CF CMF Kids Anchor Partnership Award in the amount of $91,600 for 
the FY 2027 school year. 
• Ms. Lamphier thanks Dr. Scarpati for applying for the grant and inquires about the continuation of the 
program with Dr. Allison Roy. 
• Dr. Scarpati explains the grant's purpose in finishing the work with Dr. Roy to support trust teams and 
the MTSSB social-emotional structure in schools. 
 
Ms. Lopez moved, seconded by Ms. Lewis, to approve the grant award from Crotched Mountain 
Foundation for the 2026-2029 CMF Kids Anchor Partnership Award in the amount of $91,600.00 for 
FY2027.  Motion passes 9-0. 
 
• Dr. Andrade introduces a confidential memo for approval of the MOU for an emergency shelter 
facility if needed. 
• Ms. Raymond appreciates the presentation on district security protocols and suggests a future 
presentation on updates. 
 
Mr. Johnson moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to approve the Memorandum of Understanding for an 
Emergency Shelter facility if needed. 
 
 
UNFINISHED BUSINESS 
 
LIAISON REPORTS
BOARD OF EDUCATION MEETING  August 24, 2026 
 
 
10 
PUBLIC COMMENT 
Gary Hoffman, NTU President 
• Mr. Hoffman discusses the importance of co-curricular stipends for non-athletic activities like 
yearbook, student council, band, music, drama, and literary magazines. 
• Mr. Hoffman highlights the stipends' impact on students and requests additional funding for the 
stipend committee 
Brianne Biastoff, 61B Gilman Street, Nashua 
• Ms. Biastoff, a high school music teacher, requests reconsideration of how music department stipends 
are categorized within the district stipend structure. 
• Ms. Biastoff argues that band and choral director stipends should be removed from the list of regular 
extracurricular stipends because they are integral components of their teaching positions. 
Vincent Duval, 7C Taggart Drive 
• Mr. Duval, a band director, criticizes the recent stipend committee's recommendations and the 
district's failure to recognize the work of music teachers. 
• Mr. Duval provides detailed examples of his workload and the lack of compensation compared to 
other districts. 
• Mr. Duval expresses frustration with the union's lack of advocacy and threatens to stop participating 
in extra activities if the stipends are not increased. 
 
BOARD MEMBER COMMENTS 
• Ms. Giglio, Ms. Prinn, Mr. Johnson, Ms. Lewis, and Ms. Lamphier express appreciation for the work 
of co-curricular advisors and the importance of stipends. 
• Ms. Lopez and the student board member comment on the significance of music programs and the 
need for fair compensation. 
• Ms. Raymond and Ms. Bishop reflect on the importance of back-to-school events and the need for 
better stipend practices. 
• Ms. Bishop concludes the meeting by thanking everyone for their contributions. 
 
Ms. Giglio moved, seconded by Ms. Prinn, to adjourn.  So voted at 8:09 pm. 
 
 
Submitted by Tara C. Kinsella
